observations: Photo 0 shows a black telephoto zoom lens held in a hand against a terrazzo floor.
Lens has a zoom ring, a focus ring, and what appears to be an AF/MF or stabilization switch.
Surface shows dust, grime, and some white residue/spots on the barrel.
No readable brand or model text is visible in the photo; any engraved text is too small/blurred to read.
Rear mount and front glass element are not shown, so mount type and optical condition cannot be assessed.

claims.evidence: No video or test shot showing aperture/zoom flex behavior; cannot confirm nature or severity of the fault from a still photo.

claims.claim: Implied: lens is only fit for scrap/parts
claims.evidence: Seller states intent to sell as scrap, consistent with a known flex cable fault, but no photo confirms the lens is fully non-functional versus partially usable.

risks.risk: Flex cable fault could affect aperture control, autofocus, or image stabilization, determining if any parts are salvageable.
risks.proof: A clip showing the lens mounted on a camera attempting to autofocus/zoom, or a close-up of the flex cable and contacts.

risks.risk: Front/rear glass elements could have fungus, scratches, or haze not visible in this angle.
risks.proof: Photos of front and rear glass elements under light, and through the lens held up to a bright background.
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming optics are compromised, scrap value only

risks.risk: Lens mount type and brand/model are unknown, which affects compatibility and any residual resale value for parts.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the rear mount and any engraved model text on the barrel.
risks.if_unproven: priced as generic unidentified lens, scrap/parts value

risks.risk: Physical damage (dents, cracked rings, mount pin damage) not visible from this single angle.
risks.proof: Additional photos from multiple angles, including the rear mount and lens hood area.
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming possible additional cosmetic/mechanical damage

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the rear lens mount and any engraved brand/model text.
A short video showing the lens attempting to zoom/focus and demonstrating the 'flex problem'.
Photos of front and rear glass elements for fungus/scratches.
Photo of the full lens from multiple angles to check for dents or cracks.
response.reason: The item is clearly a telephoto zoom lens with a self-declared unrepaired fault being sold as scrap; without proof of any working function or clear brand/model identification, it must be priced at worst case as a non-functional parts/scrap lens.
